summary.intent: Fix bokeh/bokeh#9129: DatePicker displays the day before the one the user just selected, for users in UTC+ (east-of-Greenwich) timezones, by changing DatePickerView._unlocal_date to derive Pikaday's displayed day from the local calendar fields of the incoming Date instead of its UTC fields; also adds a first integration-test file for the widget.
summary.issue_fit: Partial — issue-9129's reported symptom (off-by-one display after selecting a date, in UTC+ timezones) is fixed and verified. But the fix reworks _unlocal_date's general date-extraction rule rather than only the narrow post-selection round trip that caused it, which regresses the previously-correct display of any server-set value/min_date/max_date for every UTC-negative-offset (west of Greenwich) timezone; see finding date_picker.ts/_unlocal_date-negative-offset-regression.
summary.coverage: Both changed files read in full at base and head (bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts, tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py); complete diff coverage confirmed by review_context.py (2/2 diff chunks consumed, no missing chunks). Traced DatePickerView.render()/connect_signals()/_on_select()/_unlocal_date() call graph, and bokeh's Python-side date serialization (bokeh/util/serialization.py, bokeh/core/property/datetime.py, bokeh/core/json_encoder.py) to establish what shape of Date the widget actually receives from the server. Read the new test file's setup/assertions/cleanup; it is a Selenium/browser integration test which cannot execute in this offline sandbox (no browser, no npm install), so its pass/fail is unavailable evidence, but tracing shows its assertions observe the claimed behavior on the paths it covers and would not have caught the regression below (it never exercises a server-set initial value in a non-UTC browser timezone). Repository guidance checked: only .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md exists at the merge-base; no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CONTEXT.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/CODEOWNERS apply.
check_details: Reviewer ran scratch Node.js reproductions (Node v24, offline) of both the merge-base and head bodies of _unlocal_date verbatim, under TZ=Europe/Paris and TZ=America/New_York, against Date values constructed the same way bokeh's Python serializer constructs them (Date.UTC midnight) and the same way the browser reconstructs a round-tripped selection (new Date(date.toDateString())). Fresh-context verifier independently re-ran the same reproduction and confirmed the results.

The Selenium integration suite this PR adds (tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py) could not be executed: no browser or npm install is available in this offline sandbox. Traced instead; no defect found in the added assertions themselves.

findings.title: _unlocal_date now shows the wrong day for negative-UTC-offset users
findings.trigger: A DatePicker is rendered with a value/min_date/max_date coming from the server (e.g. `DatePicker(value=datetime.date.today())`, or any later Python-side `.value = some_date` assignment) while the browser's local timezone is behind UTC (`getTimezoneOffset() > 0`), e.g. any US/Canada/South America timezone.
findings.impact: bokeh's Python side always serializes a `dt.date`/`dt.datetime` value as a UTC-midnight timestamp for the intended calendar day (bokeh/util/serialization.py:182-184). Before this diff, `_unlocal_date` read that timestamp's UTC calendar day via `toISOString()`, which is correct in every timezone. This diff instead shifts the Date by `-getTimezoneOffset()` minutes first (date_picker.ts:82-85), which extracts the Date's LOCAL calendar day. For any browser timezone behind UTC, a UTC-midnight instant's local calendar day is the day before the intended one, so the picker now displays one day earlier than the actual value for a very large population of users — reintroducing the exact class of bug this PR fixes for UTC+ users, in the opposite direction, on the more basic 'display a value set from Python' path rather than only the narrower post-selection round trip the PR targets. Reproduced directly: under TZ=America/New_York, applying the merge-base body to a Date.UTC(2019,7,30,0,0,0) instant yields 'Tue Jul 30 2019' (correct); applying the head body to the same instant yields 'Mon Jul 29 2019' (wrong).
findings.change: Do not change _unlocal_date's general UTC-based extraction, which unrelated callers (the server-set value/min_date/max_date path) depend on for correctness in every timezone. Instead fix the actual defect: `_on_select` (date_picker.ts:95) stores the selected date as `date.toDateString()`, a string with no timezone marker; the next render() re-parses it with `new Date(this.model.value)` (date_picker.ts:68), which JavaScript parses as LOCAL midnight, not UTC — that mismatch, not _unlocal_date's UTC extraction, is what produced the UTC+ off-by-one. Fix that specific round trip (e.g. normalize/parse the stored string consistently, or track the picked calendar day separately from the UTC-timestamp path) so both the selection round trip and the server-set-value path read correctly in every timezone.
findings.source: issue-9129/body; commit-472e4770d363b3914bb478f0a6c3a83787b20c0d/"Fixed issue of Datepicker displaying the wrong date for users in UTC+ timezones."

observations.fact: _unlocal_date mutates its `date` argument in place (`date.setTime(...)`) before returning a new Date; every current call site passes a freshly constructed `new Date(...)` so no aliasing bug is currently observable, but the function is no longer safe to call with a shared/reused Date reference.
observations.evidence: bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:82-83, 68/70/71 (all three call sites construct `new Date(...)` inline).

requirements.evidence: date_picker.ts:82-88 fixed body, reproduced under TZ=Europe/Paris: a Date parsed from the round-tripped selection string 'Tue Jul 30 2019' now extracts to 'Tue Jul 30 2019' (was 'Mon Jul 29 2019' at merge-base), matching the day the user clicked.
